title: Hacker News Discussion on GPT-5.6 Sol Preview
description: Hacker News top story: OpenAI's preview of GPT-5.6 Sol as a next-generation model. Discussion covers government restrictions on who gets access, with Washington Post reporting U.S. government will decide GPT-5.6 access. Story trending with 831 points and 500+ comments within 8 hours of posting.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Hacker News Trends AI Assistant Hack Challenge
description: Hacker News discussion about Fernando Irarrázaval's challenge where 2,000 people tried to hack his AI assistant without success. Story trending with 351 points and 158 comments, highlighting community interest in prompt injection defenses and AI security.
author: Hacker News Community

title: CVE-2026-LGTM Incident Report Trends on Hacker News
description: Andrew Nesbitt's satirical AI security incident report about competing AI agents entering disagreement loops trends on Hacker News with 519 points and 83 comments. Community engagement highlights concerns about multi-agent systems and inference costs.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Vibe Coding Controversy on Hacker News
description: Hacker News discussion about 'Hey Nico, you didn't vibe code your data room but stole it from Papermark' - highlights ongoing community tensions around AI-generated code attribution and the ethics of 'vibe coding'. Story trending with 590 points and 275 comments.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Simon Willison on GPT-5.6 Preview and Model Pricing
description: OpenAI previewed GPT-5.6 series with three models: Sol (flagship), Terra (balanced, 2x cheaper than 5.5), and Luna (fast, affordable). New pricing: Sol $5/$30 per 1M tokens, Terra $2.50/$15, Luna $1/$6. GPT-5.6 introduces more predictable prompt caching with explicit cache breakpoints and 30-minute minimum cache life. Cache writes billed at 1.25x uncached rate, cache reads get 90% discount.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI Assistant Challenge Shows Prompt Injection Defense Improving
description: Fernando Irarrázaval's hackmyclaw.com challenge had 6,000 attempts to leak secrets from an OpenClaw test instance using Opus 4.6 - nobody succeeded. The anti-prompt-injection rules and training appear effective. Simon notes this matches his observations about labs investing in training frontier models not to fall for injection attacks, though he still wouldn't recommend production systems vulnerable to irreversible damage.
author: Simon Willison

title: CVE-2026-LGTM: Satirical AI Security Incident Report
description: Andrew Nesbitt's spectacular hypothetical incident report describes competing AI review agents entering a disagreement loop over package safety, generating 340 comments and $41,255 in inference spend before Finance revokes API keys. One vendor's marketing team issues press release about '430% YoY increase in adversarial multi-agent security reasoning' and stock rises 6%.
author: Simon Willison (via Andrew Nesbitt)

title: Semantic Early-Stopping for Iterative LLM Agent Loops
description: Introduces semantic early-stopping for iterative LLM agent loops where the loop halts when consecutive draft embeddings stop changing in meaning (measured by cosine distance with a patience parameter). Addresses the challenge of inefficient LLM agent loops that continue iterating without meaningful progress. Provides machine-checked theory and reproducible harness for validation.
author: Sahil Shrivastava

title: Joint Learning of Experiential Rules and Policies for Large Language Model Agents
description: Presents a framework for jointly learning experiential rules and policies for LLM-based agents. Focuses on how agents can accumulate and apply experiential knowledge to improve their performance over time.
author: Shicheng Ye, Chao Yu

title: Ask, Don't Judge: Binary Questions for Interpretable LLM Evaluation and Self-Improvement
description: Proposes using binary questions instead of judgments for more interpretable LLM evaluation and self-improvement. Accepted at the Second Workshop on Compositional Learning at ICML 2026. Addresses the challenge of making LLM evaluation more interpretable and actionable.
author: Sangwoo Cho, Kushal Chawla, Pengshan Cai, Zefang Liu, Chenyang Zhu, Shi-Xiong Zhang, Sambit Sahu

title: Prompt Injection in Automated Résumé Screening with Large Language Models: Single and Multi-Injection Settings
description: Analyzes prompt injection vulnerabilities in automated résumé screening systems using LLMs. Studies both single and multi-injection attack scenarios. Published in Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026.
author: Preet Baxi, Jiannan Xu, Jane Yi Jiang, Stefanus Jasin

title: Where Do CoT Training Gains Land in LLM based Agents?
description: Investigates Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning in language-model agents and examines where CoT training gains actually manifest in agent systems. Addresses findings that verbalized CoT is not always faithful, exploring the disconnect between training and deployment performance.
author: Jingyu Liu, Zhiwen Wang, Yuxin Jing, Huanyu Zhou, Yong Liu

title: Memory Depth, Not Memory Access: Selective Parametric Consolidation for Long-Running Language Agents
description: Distinguishes between memory access and memory depth as different problems. Argues that retrieval is the right tool for factual access, while selective parametric consolidation is needed for long-running language agents. Proposes methods for effectively consolidating important information into model parameters over extended operation periods.
author: Haoliang Han

title: Autoformalization of Agent Instructions into Policy-as-Code
description: Presents an autoformalization pipeline that translates agent prompts, MCP tool descriptions, and natural language policy documents into formalized policy-as-code implementations. Aims to bridge the gap between natural language instructions and executable policy code. Accepted at the Second Workshop on Agents in the Wild: Safety, Security, and Beyond (AIWILD), ICML 2026.
author: Adam Mondl, Matthew Maisel, John H. Brock

title: When Does Combining Language Models Help? A Co-Failure Ceiling on Routing, Voting, and Mixture-of-Agents Across 67 Frontier Models
description: Studies when combining language models is beneficial through routing, voting, and mixture-of-agents approaches. Evaluates across 67 frontier models and identifies a 'co-failure ceiling' - a limit beyond which model combination doesn't improve performance.
author: Josef Chen

title: AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems
description: Presents AgentX, an agent-driven self-iteration framework for industrial recommender systems. Authors listed alphabetically, suggesting a large collaborative team effort. Focuses on using agents to continuously improve and adapt recommendation systems.
author: Changxin Lao, Fei Pan, Guozhuang Ma, Han Li, Huihuang Lin, and 40+ others

title: Diagnosing Task Insensitivity in Language Agents
description: Addresses the problem of task insensitivity in language agents - when agents fail to properly adapt to different task requirements. Provides diagnostic approaches and analysis for understanding when and why language agents exhibit task-insensitive behavior.
author: Jingyu Liu, Xiaopeng Wu, Kehan Chen, Chuan Yu, Yong Liu

title: The Capability Frontier: Benchmarks Miss 82% of Model Performance
description: Argues that current benchmarks fail to capture 82% of model performance, presenting a 'capability frontier' framework. Suggests that benchmark evaluations significantly underestimate the full capabilities of AI models, leading to incomplete assessments of model performance.
author: Bradley Fowler, Ryan Smith, Daniel Thi Graviet, William Myers, Joshua Greaves, Narmeen Fatimah Oozeer, Antía García, Philip Quirke, Amirali Abdullah, Fazl Barez, Shriyash Kaustubh Upadhyay

title: Do Safety Guardrails Need to Reason? LeanGuard: A Fast and Light Approach for Robust Moderation
description: Presents LeanGuard, a fast and lightweight approach for robust moderation that questions whether safety guardrails need complex reasoning. Offers efficient moderation without heavy computational overhead, with project page and open-source code/models available.
author: Dongbin Na

title: SKILL-DISCO: Distilling and Compiling Agent Traces into Reusable Procedural Skills
description: Introduces SKILL-DISCO, a method for distilling and compiling agent traces into reusable procedural skills. Enables agents to capture and reuse procedural knowledge from their execution traces, improving efficiency and capability transfer across tasks.
author: Zhongxin Guo, Danrui Qi, Hanwen Gu, Peng Cheng, Yongqiang Xiong

title: Socratic agents for autonomous scientific discovery in high-dimensional physical systems
description: Presents Socratic agents designed for autonomous scientific discovery in high-dimensional physical systems. Uses question-driven (Socratic) approaches to explore and discover patterns in complex physical systems, with 27 pages and 5 figures detailing the methodology.
author: Xianrui Zeng, Pengfei Liu, Yirui Zang, Yang Shen, Fei Yu, Chunlei Yu, Minghao Liu, Yang Du

title: EGG: An Expert-Guided Agent Framework for Kernel Generation
description: Presents EGG, an expert-guided agent framework specifically designed for kernel generation. Combines automated agent capabilities with expert guidance to generate efficient and correct kernels for various computational tasks.
author: Yaochen Han, Ke Fan, Hongxu Jiang, Wanqi Xu, Weiyu Xie, Runhua Zhang, Chenhui Zhu, Yixiang Zhang

title: Humans Disengage, Reasoning Models Persist: Separating Difficulty Registration from Deliberation Allocation
description: Explores the difference between how humans and reasoning models allocate effort when facing difficult tasks. Humans tend to disengage from difficult problems, while reasoning models persist in deliberation. Discusses separating difficulty registration from deliberation allocation in AI systems.
author: Han-yu Wang

title: KARLA: Knowledge-base Augmented Retrieval for Language Models
description: Presents KARLA, a knowledge-base augmented retrieval approach for language models. Enhances LLM capabilities by integrating structured knowledge bases with retrieval mechanisms, improving factual accuracy and reducing hallucination.
author: Francois Crespin, Fabian M. Suchanek, Nils Holzenberger

title: German Ruling on Google AI Overview Liability
description: Bruce Schneier comments on German ruling that Google be held liable for errors in AI overviews. Key argument: AI agents are agents of the deploying organization and should be treated as such by law. If a company hired human writers, they'd be liable for inaccuracies. Allowing businesses to hide behind faulty AI excuses would be disastrous and create wrong incentives.
author: Simon Willison (via Bruce Schneier)

title: Prompt Injection as Role Confusion - Paper Analysis
description: Charles Ye, Jasmine Cui, and Dylan Hadfield-Menell present research on models struggling to distinguish privileged text in role tags (<system>, <assistant>) from untrusted user input. Models take text style more seriously than actual content. 'Destyling' text - rewriting in slightly different way - causes attack success to drop from 61% to 10%. Authors call this 'role confusion' and note injection defense remains whack-a-mole without genuine role perception.
author: Simon Willison

title: Porting Moebius 0.2B Image Inpainting to Browser with Claude Code
description: Simon ported the Moebius 0.2B image inpainting model (designed for PyTorch and NVIDIA CUDA) to run in browser using WebGPU. The 0.2B parameter model provides 10B-level performance for inpainting tasks where you mark regions to remove and model fills the space. Demo available at simonw.github.io/moebius-web/.
author: Simon Willison

title: Temporary Cloudflare Accounts for AI Agents
description: Cloudflare introduced temporary accounts feature - you can deploy Workers without creating an account using 'npx wrangler deploy --temporary'. Applications stay live for 60 minutes. Simon had GPT-5.5 build a test HTTP redirect resolver. Noted feature is marketed 'for AI agents' but interesting for everyone. Includes claim screen to extend beyond 60 minutes.
author: Simon Willison

title: Cloudflare CAPTCHA Optimization with Claude Code
description: Simon used Claude Code to optimize Cloudflare CAPTCHA rules to only trigger for search URLs with ampersands (faceted search), not simple ?q=term searches. Rule: '(http.request.uri.path wildcard "/search/*" and http.request.uri.query contains "&")'. Also tried Cloudflare MCP but it couldn't edit rules, so switched to Cloudflare API directly.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude Fable 5 Export Controls and Cyber Defense
description: Katie Moussouris clarifies that the 'jailbreak' that got Claude Fable 5 banned under export controls was simply 'fix this code' on code with known CVEs. When researchers asked Fable to 'review security issues' it refused, but 'fix this code' worked. Katie notes: 'Defenders need to be able to ask AI to fix bugs, explain why, write tests. That is not a guardrail bypass - it's the most valuable thing an AI model can do for defensive security.'
author: Simon Willison (via Katie Moussouris)
